title: Specification-Aware Predictive Uncertainty Decomposition
abstract: arXiv:2611.02956v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Classical decompositions of predictive uncertainty, such as the information-theoretic one, are defined for a fixed representation $x$ of the input object. They do not consider that $x$ may be incomplete, nor do they measure how much the missing information can affect the prediction. In Large Language Models, users can clarify an underspecified input without any retraining. The clarified input can describe the user's unobserved intent $z^*$ more accurately and change the predictive uncertainty about the outcome. In this paper, we formalize this setting probabilistically and derive a three-term decomposition of prediction risk into specification, residual aleatoric, and epistemic uncertainties. We show that at the original information level, when only $x$ is available, the aleatoric uncertainty, represented by a Bayes risk, has two components. translated_title: 规范感知的预测不确定性分解
translated_abstract: 经典的预测不确定性分解方法（例如信息论分解）是针对输入对象的固定表示 $x$ 定义的。这些方法既没有考虑 $x$ 可能是不完整的，也没有衡量缺失的信息会对预测产生多大影响。在大语言模型中，用户无需任何重新训练即可澄清欠规范的输入。澄清后的输入能够更准确地描述用户未被观测到的意图 $z^*$，并改变对结果的预测不确定性。本文从概率角度对这一设定进行了形式化，并推导出将预测风险分解为三项的方案：规范不确定性、残余偶然不确定性和认知不确定性。我们证明，在原始信息水平上（即仅有 $x$ 可用时），以贝叶斯风险表示的偶然不确定性包含两个组成部分。第一个组成部分——我们称之为规范不确定性——是该贝叶斯风险的期望缩减量。
tldr: 本文提出一种规范感知的预测不确定性分解方法，将预测风险分解为规范不确定性、残余偶然不确定性和认知不确定性三项，从而量化了在大语言模型中通过澄清欠规范输入（补全用户意图）能够减少多少预测不确定性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a specification-aware decomposition of predictive uncertainty that splits prediction risk into specification, residual aleatoric, and epistemic uncertainties, quantifying how clarifying an underspecified input (e.g., in LLMs) reduces predictive uncertainty.
